patch.value: Continuous invariant fuzzing: randomized operation sequences checked against declared workspace, history, and graph invariants

The suite proves that specified operations produce specified results. It does not systematically attack the space of operation SEQUENCES, which is where a data-integrity engine actually fails: an interleaving of create, close, restore, redact, compact, merge, schema change, and config change that leaves a hash chain unverifiable, an edge pointing at a tombstone, a derived index disagreeing with authoritative files, or a claim held by nobody but not released. Declare the invariants that must hold after any sequence — the hash chain verifies; every declared edge resolves or is explicitly a tombstone reference; derived artifacts agree with authoritative files or are marked stale; lifecycle state is reachable from the recorded history; no item is unreconstructable from its stream — and then generate randomized sequences against them, with shrinking so a failure produces a minimal reproducer and a seed that reproduces it exactly. This complements rather than duplicates the seeded fault and concurrency harness: that harness injects failures into interleavings, this one explores operation sequences under normal conditions. Every discovered violation becomes a filed item with its minimal reproducer as a permanent regression fixture.

The invariant set is declared explicitly as data — chain verifiability, edge resolvability, derived-artifact agreement, lifecycle reachability, per-item reconstructability — with each invariant naming what violates it; Randomized sequences cover create, update, close, restore, delete, redact, compact, merge, schema change, and config change in arbitrary orders; A violation produces a minimal shrunk reproducer plus a seed that reproduces it deterministically; Every violation found is filed as an item with its reproducer added to the permanent regression corpus, linked discovered_from this item; The suite runs on a schedule with a time budget rather than blocking every change, and a violation opens work immediately rather than being retried; Coverage over the declared invariant set is reported, so an invariant no sequence has ever attacked is visible as a gap
The engine's invariants are attacked continuously by sequences no author would think to write
Every claim pm makes — immutable history, restorable state, verifiable chains, correct graphs — is an invariant claim, and invariant claims are only as strong as the adversary that has tested them
Adds a long-running randomized suite whose failures are, by construction, real integrity defects; requires the invariant set to be declared explicitly for the first time
Integrity defects are found by machine before a workspace hits them, with a minimal reproducer attached

message: File invariant fuzzing — the suite tests operations, not the sequence space where integrity actually breaks
